name: IanWalksMumbai
description:
IanWalksMumbai is your invitation to discover the city the way Ian did—on foot, with curiosity, humor, and a healthy respect for potholes. Expect vivid histories, unexpected detours, and probably a snack stop or three. You won’t just see Mumbai—you’ll feel it, taste it, laugh with it… and maybe get a little lost with Ian (on purpose).

Ready to walk? Let’s go.

featured_reviews.name: Cassandra R
featured_reviews.review_text: I booked a full day tour with Ian and couldn’t have had a better guide to show me all over Mumbai. He was on time, curated my experience to my tastes, so full of information, and a welcoming host. He met me at my hotel, arranged for a driver, sweated in 43°, and never slowed down. I tasted food safely, felt safe as a solo woman traveler, never felt forced into buying anything I didn’t. It was truly an experience of a lifetime and I’m so very grateful. Thank you Ian!
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Thank you so much for such a wonderful review, Cassandra 😊

It was an absolute pleasure spending the day exploring Mumbai with you. I’m so glad you enjoyed the experience and that we were able to tailor the day around your interests in food, history, local culture, and everyday life in the city.

I'm especially happy to hear that you felt comfortable and safe throughout the tour. As a solo traveler visiting India for the first time, I know that can be a big consideration, and it means a lot to hear that you felt welcomed and at ease.

We certainly picked a warm day for sightseeing! 😅 But it was great fun discovering so many different sides of Mumbai together — from heritage landmarks and bustling markets to local food stops and hidden stories along the way.

I also genuinely enjoyed our conversations throughout the day. Meeting curious travelers from different parts of the world is one of my favourite parts of what I do, and I learned a lot from our discussions as well.

Thank you again for your kind words and for trusting me to show you around the city. It was a pleasure meeting you, and I'm delighted that your day in Mumbai was such a memorable one.

Safe travels, and you’ll always have a friend in Mumbai when you return!

IanWalksMumbai

featured_reviews.name: An G
featured_reviews.review_text:
We went for a heritage walk in CSMT with Ian late-September, and it was a blast!

He’s energetic, well-informed and convivial!

The walk took about 2 hours — wherein we explored the exterior and interior architectural aspects of the iconic train station. Throughout the walk, Ian regaled us with stories of historical significance, and even quizzed us a bit along the way! It was very engaging.

We made a stop at the train museum inside the station - a modest setup with a LOT of paraphernalia for rail transport enthusiasts!

Before we did this walk - We really didn’t know how much the station had to offer, despite living in Mumbai for some time now.

Walks like these are a lovely way to get acquainted with the city. An experience made all the richer with an enthusiastic and passionate guide like Ian!

We look forward to joining him for another heritage walk sometime! Thank you for a memorable time.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Thank you so much for the wonderful review and the kind words, An! 🙏

I’m so glad you'll enjoyed the CSMT Heritage Walk — it was so much fun exploring Mumbai’s most iconic landmark together. I loved how curious and engaged you were throughout! It means a lot that you appreciated the stories and the details that make this building so special.

Hope to see you'll again soon on another Mumbai heritage walk! 🌆

IanWalksMumbai

featured_reviews.name: Obada
featured_reviews.review_text: We took an evening tour fir the south of Mumbai. The trip with Ian was very informative, engaging and interesting. The fact that it's a private free walking tour is really unique and offers a lot of flexibility in terms of the tour's timing and topics in focus. Highly recommended.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Thank you so much, Obada! 😊

I’m really glad you enjoyed the evening walking tour in South Mumbai. Sharing the city through stories in a relaxed, engaging way is what these walks are all about, and I’m happy to hear you appreciated the flexibility and personal nature of the experience.

The idea behind keeping it a private, free walking tour is to let conversations, interests, and curiosity shape the walk rather than a fixed script. Thank you for the strong recommendation, and I hope to walk with you again soon on another IanWalksMumbai tour!

featured_reviews.name: Rajdeep Maity
featured_reviews.review_text: I've visited CSMT countless times growing up, but I never really understood its architecture until this tour. Seeing it through Ian's explanation changed the entire experience. The way you broke things down made the details easy to follow, and the way you told the stories behind the place kept it engaging instead of feeling like a history lecture. I walked away actually appreciating the structure instead of just passing by it. Overall, the tour was genuinely fun and surprisingly eye-opening
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Thank you so much, Rajdeep! 🙏

It means a lot to hear this—especially from someone who has grown up around CSMT. One of my favourite parts of guiding the CSMT Heritage Walk is helping people see the station in a completely new light, and I’m really glad the stories, architecture breakdowns, and little details helped make the experience engaging instead of feeling like a history lesson.

Hearing that you walked away appreciating the building in a whole new way is truly the best compliment. Thank you for joining the tour and for sharing such a thoughtful review. Hope to explore more of Mumbai’s heritage with you again someday! 😊

IanWalksMumbai

featured_reviews.name: Ananya Nayak
featured_reviews.review_text:
On Saturday, 6th of December I took a tour of CSMT with Ian. When I had booked the tour (available in BMS) I was only interested in the gigantic magnificent buildings. But Ian, made me look and understand them. This person is nostalgic and passionate about the history and buildings. He not only recites the history, he connects the dots to the present.

He quizzes you on things, makes it interactive and introspective and is very friendly. He narrates fun incidents happening over different times and isn't afraid to admit that there are few things that he isn't very aware of.

The walk is designed to have a look at almost everything, including a reclusive Railway Museum which isn't other wise opened to the public. He also recommends other tours, areas to explore and much more.

I would definitely recommend this tour.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Thank you so much, Ananya!😊

I’m really glad you joined the CSMT tour and even happier that it helped you see the building beyond its grandeur. It means a lot when someone appreciates the connections between past and present—that’s exactly why I love sharing these stories.

I’m thrilled you enjoyed the interactive style, the quizzes, and the lesser-known spots like the Railway Museum. And thank you for noticing the honesty and passion behind the walk—that truly made my day.

Really appreciate the recommendation, and I hope we get to explore more of Mumbai together soon! 😊

IanWalksMumbai

featured_reviews.review_text: Ian led our tour of CSMT in Mumbai, including areas of the grand railway office building that are off limits to the public. He kept the tour fun and engaging, and covered a LOT of ground in a short time: colonial history, architecture, commerce and all the other influences on this spectacular structure.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Thank you so much, Krishnan! 🙏

I’m really glad you enjoyed the CSMT heritage tour — especially the chance to explore the exclusive areas inside the old railway headquarters. It’s such an incredible building, and I’m happy the mix of history, architecture, and stories came together in a way that felt engaging for you.

I truly appreciate you joining the walk and taking the time to share this wonderful review. Hope to see you again on another Mumbai adventure!

IanWalksMumbai

featured_reviews.name: Anuradha Bhave
featured_reviews.review_text: When we say kokan, mostly beautiful beaches, and old style houses surrounded by coconut, mango, and cashew trees comes to everyone's mind. But the trip that we took with Girispandan was different in many ways. We got to experience a beautiful evening boat ride on a sangam point where 3 rivers met and witnessed the most beautiful evening sky displaying colour shades, which could not be captured by camera. The entire trip unfolded many aspects of the Kokan region with beautiful old temples, Katal Shilpa, Kashtha Shilpa museum, and amazing stay at Rai resort. This place truly lives up to its name, helping us experience what it's like to be one with nature and live in a place that is completely surrounded by endless trees and various species of birds. Last but not the least, the trip being Aamra Mahotsav, from the very first meal till the last we got to taste endless variety of Mango dishes and the actual naturally ripen mangoes along with many more other local culinary masterpieces that left us speechless. Many thanks to Girispandan  - Parag Dada and Bapat Sir and Mr. Amol and Mrs. Manek and their entire team from Rai resort for the greatest hospitality and an unforgettable experience. I'm looking forward to many more such trips with Girispandan.

And it turned out to be such a good decision because the experience was extremely insightful and fun. The walk tour was very well-planned and on time. Tanmay shared in detail deep facets of every place visited;  his narration entailed stories of the Erstwhile Bombay, the current relevance and status. He deftly switched into English, Hindi, Marathi to cater to his audience and used wit and humour which made the walk and talk refreshing. Leena, as his resourceful partner, ensured that the arrangements were in place and made us very comfortable, providing snippets of the places from her end too.
All in all, a great experience and worth recommending!

featured_reviews.review_text: Being my first trek at the age of 50 I was not sure if I should go ahead with it, but Mr. Sandesh Lad assured that I would be fine and trek trained Ms. Tejasvi would take good care of us. His assuring words turned truth when Mr. Chandrakant (Pappu) and Ms. Tejasvi ensured that I was comfortable through the Trek as I had to take longer breaks because of steep stone paths and some patches of steep climb. featured_reviews.name: Rachana Thakar
featured_reviews.review_text:
HEAVEN FOR REAL #Letsgo

14/12/2017-17/12/2017
The best decision of joining the Digital Detoxification trip by Let’s Go Outdoors
I never knew that such a beautiful world exists until I decided to go for digital detox with let's go and explored the mesmerizing beauties of nature.
My first ever trip.
Uttarakhand,Jim Corbett

Meeting a group of unknown people who are no more unknown to me.
Traveling on beautiful roads of Delhi to Uttarakhand.
Reaching Jim Corbett and then walking towards Eco Resort for 45mins brought butterflies in my stomach of every surprise on the way. Crossing the river on a small raft made me happy like a kid.
Cool breeze hitting my face,sound of the river and birds made me feel so close to the nature. There I see the beautiful place where we will stay in the middle  of the forest welcoming me with wide open arms to experience the most amazing next 2days of my life.
Never thought mornings can be so beautiful in the forests and mountains where all you see is loving nature.
The lovely staff of the resort made us extremely happy by the service provided. The yummiest and healthy food they served and how can I forget the smiles on their faces after seeing us happy.
The experience of star gazing, bird watching, spotting animals like barking deer, sambar, lungurs, brown fish owl, vultures and many more. Sitting near the river side made me realise we are so unaware about our beautiful places and nature in our country. But not any more. I promised myself sitting near the river that I want to see more, learn more and LIVE MORE.
Today this is a ‘SUPER HAPPY ME’ after realising that we really must leave our phones and all the gadgets aside and live and enjoy the beautiful experiences, which cannot be captured by any camera of this world. It can only be felt.
In the end I am so grateful to Sandesh for taking me to such a beautiful place.
Memories for life☺

featured_reviews.name: Ritesh K R
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kondivite Caves (Mahakali Caves) are one of Mumbai’s most underrated historical gems—quiet, raw, and deeply rooted in India’s ancient Buddhist past.

Dating back to around the 2nd century BCE, these rock-cut caves began in the Hinayana tradition and later saw influences of the Mahayana phase, remaining active up to around the 6th century CE and even beyond till the 12th century in some form. You can actually sense this long continuity as you walk through the caves—simple early structures evolving into more developed spaces.

Carved out of basalt rock and once surrounded by dense forests, the setting would have been ideal for monks—isolated, peaceful, and close to natural water sources. Like Bhaje and Karle caves, the site reflects how geography and trade routes shaped spiritual centres.

The presence of Pali inscriptions adds another layer of authenticity and historical depth, connecting you directly to the lives and practices of the monks who once lived here.

Today, the caves still carry a quiet, meditative energy, though the surroundings could definitely be cleaner and better maintained. More signage or guided interpretation would really help visitors appreciate the historical context.

Overall, a fascinating visit—especially if you enjoy history, archaeology, or simply discovering hidden layers of Mumbai beyond its modern chaos.

featured_reviews.name: Abhijeet Thigale
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Mahakali Caves (historically known as the Kondivite Caves) are a hidden archaeological treasure tucked away in the bustle of Andheri East, Mumbai.
​Whether you're a history buff or just looking for a pocket of peace in the city, here is a review of this ancient site.
​The Experience: A Step Back in Time
​The Mahakali Caves are a group of 19 rock-cut Buddhist monuments dating from the 1st Century BCE to the 6th Century CE. Carved directly into solid black basalt rock, these caves served as a quiet retreat for Buddhist monks long before Mumbai became a financial hub.
​The Architecture
​Cave 9 (The Main Attraction): This is the largest and most significant cave. It features a Chaitya (prayer hall) with a stupa and a unique semicircular wall. Look closely at the walls—even though they have weathered over 2,000 years, you can still see mutilated figures of Buddha and characters from Buddhist mythology.
​The Viharas: The other caves are mostly Viharas (monasteries). These are small, stark cells where monks lived and meditated. Their simplicity is a powerful contrast to the modern skyscrapers visible in the distance.
​The View: Located on a small hill, the site offers a panoramic view of the Jogeshwari-Vikhroli Link Road (JVLR). It’s a surreal experience to stand in a 2,000-year-old monastery while watching the "maximum city" rush by below.

we did the essential Mumbai tour with Parvez. he was a great guide for a great trip. The tour started off near the Asiatic society, and we walked around the area originally inside the Fort walls. featured_reviews.review_text: We visited the BMC Headquarters with Khaki Tours on 25th May, and it was an absolutely awesome experience! featured_reviews.review_text: We had arranged for a group tour of Castle 2 Gateway through Khakee Tour. It was the best experience we ever had. featured_reviews.name: Max Mackie
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mumbai history comes alive! An amazing walk with Surabhi.

I recently took the Fort area heritage walk with Khaki Tours, and I cannot recommend it enough. Our guide, Surabhi, was absolutely fantastic.
It wasn’t just a recitation of dates and facts; Surabhi is a natural storyteller. She wove together the history of colonial Bombay with fascinating anecdotes about the architecture and the people who built this city. She pointed out hidden details in the Gothic buildings that I would have walked right past without noticing.

Her energy was contagious, and she was incredibly patient in answering all our questions. Whether you are a tourist or a local Mumbaikar, you will see the Fort area with completely new eyes after this. If you book a Khaki Tour, definitely ask for Surabhi!

Tour Highlights:

Marine Drive at Dawn: Begin your tour at Marine Drive, also known as the “Queen’s Necklace.” Experience the tranquility of this iconic promenade as the city gradually awakens.
Gateway of India: Witness the majestic Gateway of India in the soft morning light and learn about its historical significance.
Flora Fountain: Discover the exquisite architecture of Flora Fountain, a beautiful heritage structure in the heart of Mumbai.
Crawford Market: Experience the bustling atmosphere of Crawford Market as vendors set up their stalls and locals shop for fresh produce and flowers.
Breakfast at Irani Cafes: Savor a traditional Parsi breakfast at one of Mumbai’s iconic Irani cafes, where the city’s morning rituals come alive.
Mumbai’s Religious Diversity: Visit a local temple, mosque, or church, and observe the morning prayers, reflecting Mumbai’s diverse and harmonious communities.
Victoria Terminus (VT) at Sunrise: Marvel at the grandeur of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus as the morning sun illuminates its magnificent architecture.
